liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Keith joins Jerry energetically at the end of the first Dark Star section for a rollicking jam; Dark Star with the surprise Top of the World jam inside runs nearly half an hour [7][9][17]
- **Sittin' On Top Of The World** (2 reviews): Reviewer considers this a great version of the song, played rarely; Reviewer finds this version intense and wonders why the band stopped playing it [8][17]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer notes this was only the second Jack Straw ever played, with striking echoing, distorted guitar from Jerry [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Frozen Logger**: rare: 9 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-10-21.sbd.miller.112086.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 155 min; rated 4.25/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd71-10-21.sbd.cotsman.5071.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 142 min; rated 4.36/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard sound excellent for 1971; Reviewer calls the mix album-ready with quality audio; Described as a well-balanced Betty mix, with a secondary mix done separately [8][11][18]
- **gd1971-10-21.sbd.bertha-ashley.9622.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 143 min; rated 4.29/5 by 7 [3]
- **gd1971-10-21.168695.fm.wolfe.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: FM broadcast; 24 songs; 143 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- Pigpen is absent, reportedly ill; Weir announces from the stage that he is not there [12]
- Keith Godchaux is the new keyboardist, and an organ part resembling Pigpen's is audible [12]
- Keith Godchaux plays Pigpen's organ rather than piano, at what the reviewer believes was his second show [14]
- Reviewer says Keith was about 22 or 23 and could play organ and piano simultaneously [15]
- Jerry's joke refers to the Dead's habit of pricing tickets a dollar or two under comparable artists [18]
- Reviewer says this was Keith's second show and first Dark Star with the band [7]
- Reviewer notes Dark Stars were scarce in 1971 and compares the show favorably with 10/19, which introduced many new songs [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-10-21.sbd.miller.112086.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat [1]. Also: Recording credited to David Gans [1]
- **gd71-10-21.sbd.cotsman.5071.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> MR> C> D> CD> EAC>S HN [2]. Also: Reviewer's first Dead tape was a reel-to-reel recording off WGLD Oak Park/Chicago radio [18]
- **gd1971-10-21.sbd.bertha-ashley.9622.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: SBD>>MR>>Cass>>DAT>>CDA>>SHN>>DAW(Bertha)>>CDA [3]. Also: Remastered March 4, 2002 on a dual-DAW system called Bertha; minor clipping corrected first; Original transfer and SHN encoding by Scott Clugston [3]
- **gd1971-10-21.168695.fm.wolfe.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Don Wolfe; transferred by Matt Smith, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: FM Broadcast (WGLD 102.7 FM - Oak Park, IL) > ?? > Don Wolfe's Reels [5]
